title: A Will for the Alibi
premise: True-crime podcaster Isandro Nystrom is hired by a dying woman, Maren Voss, who pays a fortune to prove that her brother — missing for thirty years and presumed drowned — has not yet been murdered, because his body was never found. Isandro's investigation reveals the 'cold case' was staged: the disappearance was faked to protect Maren from a violent husband, but someone in their found-family circle has been quietly waiting three decades for the tide to give up the evidence. As Isandro closes in, the would-be killer moves to finish what the sea wouldn't, forcing her to choose between exposing the truth and protecting the only family Maren has left. In the end, Isandro proves the murder hasn't happened by preventing it, closing the case on her own terms — justice delivered outside the law.
about_author: E. M. Lockridge is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing coastal cold cases before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about people who refuse to let the water keep its secrets.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid for Nothing
chapters.summary: Isandro Nystrom's POV. A frail woman named Maren Voss arrives at the studio with an envelope of cash: prove my brother hasn't been murdered yet. Isandro, who never takes a case she can't close, almost refuses — until Maren mentions the tide. The beat is wary curiosity sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Salt
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She digs into the 1995 disappearance of Tomas Voss, lost off Gullwrack Point, body never recovered. The official file is thin, suspiciously tidy. An interview with the retired harbor master yields one anomaly: Tomas's boat was found anchored, not adrift. Beat: the first crack in the official story.

chapters.title: Rules of the Show
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, interwoven with podcast narration. She lays out her method on air — alibis are stories, and stories age badly. Listeners write in with memories of that night; one letter claims Tomas was seen alive two days after he drowned. Beat: the case stops being history and becomes a living thing.

chapters.title: Maren's House of Small Truths
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Visiting Maren at the coastal care home, Isandro notices photographs cropped to remove one person: Maren's late husband, Aldous. Maren deflects every question about him with practiced calm. Beat: tenderness laced with dread — Isandro realizes Maren is afraid of something other than grief.

chapters.title: The Alibi That Held Too Well
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Reconstructing the night of the disappearance, she finds four witnesses whose accounts align perfectly — too perfectly, matching down to weather details they couldn't have known. Someone coached them. Beat: the thrill of the hunt curdling into unease.

chapters.title: Found Family
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She tracks the four witnesses: a fisherman, a nurse, a teacher, and Maren's old friend Dev, now a boat restorer. They were all, once, a tight circle around the Voss siblings. Dev warns her off with genuine warmth — and genuine fear. Beat: loyalty as both shield and cage.

chapters.title: What the Harbor Master Kept
chapters.summary: Harbor master Elias Rook's POV (flashback to 1995). He saw Aldous Voss scrubbing blood from a deck at dawn and chose silence, believing he was protecting Maren. Present-day coda: Rook mails Isandro a key. Beat: guilt as a slow poison across decades.

chapters.title: The Key
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The key opens a harbor locker holding Tomas's recovered satchel — dry-bagged, hidden, never logged. Inside: letters proving Tomas planned to flee with Maren from Aldous's abuse, and a forged death certificate draft. Beat: revelation that reframes everything — the drowning was staged to free Maren.

chapters.title: A Murder That Hasn't Happened
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. If the death was fake, why does Maren fear a murder? Isandro replays Maren's phrasing and lands on it: someone believes Tomas will resurface now that Aldous is dead, and means to make the old lie permanent. Beat: horror dawning — she isn't investigating a past crime, she's standing inside a future one.

chapters.title: Dev's Silence
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev confesses to the reader, if not yet to Isandro: he helped stage the disappearance, and he knows which member of their circle never forgave Tomas for leaving — or believed Aldous deserved worse than a fake death. Beat: love and complicity braided together.

chapters.title: The Letter Writer
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Tracing the anonymous listener letter claiming a post-disappearance sighting, she finds it came from within the circle — sent weeks after Maren contacted the show. Someone has been watching Isandro's progress like a countdown. Beat: paranoia tightening; the hunter learns she is hunted.

chapters.title: Storm Season
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A storm damages the Gullwrack seawall, and locals speak of what the erosion might uncover. Isandro realizes the coast itself is the clock: if bones surface, the staged death becomes provable murder. Beat: nature as antagonist, urgency rising.

chapters.title: The Nurse's Ledger
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The witness-nurse, Ilsa, finally talks: Aldous didn't die naturally. His hospice records were altered, and the person with access was family-adjacent — someone in the circle. Beat: the found family contains its own rot; trust fractures.

chapters.title: Two Funerals
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At a memorial for Aldous, the whole circle gathers under one roof for the first time in thirty years. Isandro watches them: grief, relief, and one face performing all three. She narrows her suspect to the teacher, Corwin Hale. Beat: quiet menace at a social gathering.

chapters.title: Corwin's Perfect Memory
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She confronts Corwin with the coached-alibi timeline. He is urbane, unshakeable — until she quotes the weather detail no witness could know firsthand. His composure slips for exactly one second. Beat: cat-and-mouse where the mouse smiles.

chapters.title: Maren Breaks
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren admits everything to Isandro: the abuse, the staged escape, and her terror that Corwin — Aldous's protégé and the circle's devoted keeper — has spent thirty years waiting to bury the truth along with Tomas, should Tomas ever come home. Beat: catharsis and dread entwined.

chapters.title: Where the Tide Keeps Its Word
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Storm erosion exposes remains near Gullwrack Point — but forensics suggest they're animal, placed deliberately. Corwin planted a decoy to draw out whoever was digging. Which means he knows Isandro is close. Beat: trap snapping shut.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Appointment
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A message lures her alone to the decommissioned Gullwrack light: proof of where Tomas actually went. It's Corwin, and he intends for Isandro to become the case's final casualty — a podcaster lost to the sea chasing ghosts. Beat: peak danger, isolation, courage.

chapters.title: What Dev Buried
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating Isandro/Dev POVs. Dev, following his conscience at last, arrives mid-struggle; the truth spills out — Tomas is alive, living quietly abroad, and Corwin's obsession was never justice but possession of the story. Together they subdue Corwin as the storm breaks. Beat: violence, loyalty redeemed, truth triumphant.

chapters.title: Proof of Life
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A video call: Tomas Voss, older, weathered, alive. He chose exile so Maren could be free of Aldous without a murder trial shadowing her. Isandro must decide whether airing this serves justice or destroys the peace thirty years bought. Beat: moral weight settling on her shoulders.

chapters.title: Off the Record
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She closes the case without naming Tomas publicly — the episode airs as the story of a staged escape and a predator's long patience, identities protected. Corwin faces charges for the hospice falsification and the lighthouse attack. Beat: justice outside the law, chosen deliberately.

chapters.title: The Tide Gives Back
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, epilogue. Maren, reunited by phone with her brother, asks Isandro how she can ever repay her. Isandro, who always closes her cases, says the payment was watching a family survive its own secret. On Gullwrack beach, the tide recedes clean. Beat: peace earned, found family affirmed.
